summary: The exact candidate prevents the deterministically reproduced event-loop starvation mechanism, but regresses established Prometheus exposition behavior by dropping name[] filtering, gzip encoding negotiation, and OpenMetrics content negotiation. It is a partial fix that requires changes, and the original distributed H100 PD failure remains unverified in this ROCm single-GPU environment.

tests.what_was_measured: On the recorded base, a 350 ms delay in the actual Prometheus ASGI bake path caused 331 ms of event-loop lag, reproducing the reported starvation mechanism.
At exact candidate commit, four focused mocked tests passed for isolation/singleflight, timeout cleanup, child failure, and cancellation cleanup.
Candidate regression returned 200 for the active scrape, 503 for the concurrent scrape, and measured 0.000 seconds event-loop lag.
Independent health/isolation behavior passed (health 200, 0.001 s lag, overlapping scrape 503), but name[] filtering, gzip negotiation, and OpenMetrics content negotiation were all absent.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU was used because this defect and patch are confined to CPU-side ASGI scheduling and Prometheus multiprocess-file exposition. The available architecture was gfx950/ROCm 7.2, not the reported eight-H100 CUDA topology.

remaining_counterexamples: GET /metrics?name[]=alpha_total returns unrelated beta_total output because the candidate ignores Prometheus name[] filtering.
GET /metrics with Accept-Encoding: gzip returns no Content-Encoding because the candidate bypasses exposition compression negotiation.
GET /metrics with Accept: application/openmetrics-text returns Prometheus text 0.0.4 rather than negotiated OpenMetrics output.
remaining_limitations: The original eight-H100 multi-node single-tokenizer PD deployment, real concurrent scrape pressure, bootstrap read timeouts, and decode-side connection-loss logs were not reproduced.
The prepared environment is ROCm 7.2 with one gfx950 GPU; it cannot qualify the reported CUDA/H100 distributed topology.
The deterministic fixture validates the shared-event-loop starvation mechanism and overload response, not a full model, semantic accuracy, or distributed workload.
No native code changed and repository-environment.json declares no native artifact, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
